| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| κρατερὸς Διομήδης (4.401, 4.411) | "strong Diomedes" | "strong Diomedes" | "mighty" (reserved for ἴφθιμος), "stout", "valiant" (reserved for ἄλκιμος), "brave"; κρατερός keeps the table's "strong" (κρατερὸν μῦθον "a strong word", 1.25) |
| τὸν δ’ ἄρ’ ὑπόδρα ἰδὼν προσέφη κρατερὸς Διομήδης (4.411, whole-line reply-formula) | "Him then with a scowl looking addressed strong Diomedes:" | "Then strong Diomedes, looking at him with a scowl, spoke to him:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); built on the Odyssey table's τὸν δ’ ἄρ’ ὑπόδρα ἰδὼν προσέφη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς (8.165) with κρατερὸς Διομήδης from the row above |
| τὸν δ’ υἱὸς Καπανῆος ἀμείψατο κυδαλίμοιο (4.403, whole-line reply-formula; Sthenelus unnamed) | "And him answered the son of glorious Capaneus:" | "Then the son of glorious Capaneus answered him:" | naming "Sthenelus" (the Greek does not); "renowned" (kept for ἀγακλειτός, 2.564), "famous" (κλυτός); κυδάλιμος keeps the Odyssey's "glorious" and agrees with Καπανῆος, not with υἱός |
| καί μιν φωνήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (4.369; departure from 1.201 in the pronoun only) | "and, lifting his voice, to him winged words he spoke:" | "and lifting his voice he spoke winged words to him:" | "to her" (the published English of 1.201, where μιν is Athena; here μιν is Diomedes); the unit is joined to 4.368 so that the whole-unit rule does not force the wrong pronoun, as at 2.7 and 4.312 |
| ὣς εἰπὼν τοὺς μὲν λίπεν αὐτοῦ, βῆ δὲ μετ’ ἄλλους (4.364 = 4.292) | published (iliad-024) | published | none; the unit takes the shipped English of 4.292 unchanged, though the edition ends 364 with a full stop and 292 with an ano teleia (so `l` and `i` end in a semicolon) |
| ὑπέρθυμος (Διομήδεα, 4.365) | "high-spirited" | "high-spirited" | "great-hearted" (reserved for μεγάθυμος), "overweening"; follows the Odyssey table's ὑπέρθυμος |
| ἱππηλάτα Τυδεύς (4.387) | "horse-driver Tydeus" | "Tydeus the horse-driver" | "horseman" (reserved for ἱππότα), "horse-taming" (ἱππόδαμος); follows the Odyssey table's γέρων ἱππηλάτα Νέστωρ |
| κέντορες ἵππων (Καδμεῖοι κέντορες ἵππων, 4.391) | "goaders of horses" | "goaders of horses" | "horsemen", "charioteers", "horse-tamers" (reserved for ἱππόδαμος); κέντωρ is from κεντέω "prick, goad", and the epithet is kept as a noun with its genitive |
| Ἀσωπὸν … βαθύσχοινον λεχεποίην (4.383) | "the Asopus, deep-rushed, grass-bedded" | "the Asopus, deep in rushes, with its beds of grass" | "reedy", "rush-grown", "marshy" for βαθύσχοινος (each drops βαθύς "deep" or decides the plant); λεχεποίης follows the Iliad table's λεχεποίης "grass-bedded" / "with its beds of grass" (2.697) |
| πυκινὸν λόχον (4.392) | "a solid ambush" | "a solid ambush" | "close ambush", "thick ambush", "dense", "shrewd" (πυκινὴ βουλή); πυκινός keeps the Odyssey table's "solid" (πυκινὸς δόμος, πυκινὰ μήδεα) |
| παραίσια σήματα (4.381) | "unfitting signs" | "unfitting signs" | "unfavourable", "ominous", "adverse", "unlucky" (each decides the sense); παραίσιος is the opposite of ἐναίσιμος "fitting" (2.353), and the note says the signs are of ill omen |
| βίης Ἐτεοκληείης (4.386) | "the might of Eteocles" | "the might of Eteocles" | "mighty Eteocles", "Eteocles himself" (each erases the periphrasis); follows βίη Ἡρακληείη "the might of Heracles" (2.658) and Πριάμοιο βίην "the might of Priam" (3.105) |
| Καδμεΐωνες · Καδμεῖοι (4.385, 4.388, 4.391) | "Cadmeans" · "Cadmeans" | "Cadmeans" · "Cadmeans" | "Thebans" (kept for the men of Θήβη), "sons of Cadmus"; both forms are the same people and keep one English |
| Πολυνείκης (4.377) | "Polynices" | "Polynices" | "Polyneices", "Polunices"; the familiar Latinised form, as for the other Greek names |
| ξεῖνος (of Tydeus, 4.377, 4.387) | "stranger" | "stranger" | "guest" (the table keeps "guest-friend" for ξεῖνος of the bond, 9.18), "foreigner", "visitor"; the Odyssey's ξεῖνε "stranger" |
| ἐπίρροθος (4.390) | "helper" | "helper" | "ally" (reserved for ἐπίκουρος), "champion", "supporter"; a rare word, the note gives the sense only |
| ἀεθλεύειν προκαλίζετο (4.389) | "kept challenging them to contend in contests" | "kept challenging them to compete in contests" | "to games" (the Odyssey table's ἄεθλος "contest" is kept), "to wrestle", "to a trial of skill"; προκαλίζομαι "challenge" |
| ἐπιείκελος ἀθανάτοισιν (Μαίων, 4.394) | "resembling the immortals" | "like the immortals" | "godlike" (reserved for ἀντίθεος); follows the Odyssey table (15.414) |
| ἔπεφνε (4.397) | "killed" | "killed" | "slew" (the Odyssey's `l` at odyssey-014; `i` and `l` at odyssey-055 have "killed", which is followed), "destroyed"; the aorist of φένω |
| εἷο χέρεια … ἀμείνω (4.400) | "than himself worse … better" | "worse than himself … better" | "inferior", "weaker" for χέρεια; "superior" for ἀμείνω (reserved for κρείσσων); χέρεια / χερείων keeps "worse" (as in χερειότερον, 2.248) and ἀμείνων "better" |
| μάχῃ · ἀγορῇ (4.400) | "in fighting" · "in assembly" | "in fighting" · "in assembly" | "in war", "in battle" (kept for the Odyssey's μάχη "fight" / "battle" in other contexts); "in counsel", "in speech"; ἀγορή keeps "assembly" and the note says the sense is skill in speaking |
| αἰδεσθεὶς βασιλῆος ἐνιπὴν αἰδοίοιο (4.402) | "having respected the rebuke of the revered king" | "respecting the rebuke of the revered king" | "ashamed before" (αἰδέομαι also means "be ashamed"), "in awe of", "out of respect for" (each decides the force); αἰδέομαι keeps "respect" (αἰδεῖσθαι ἱερῆα, 1.23); αἰδοῖος "revered" as in the Odyssey table |
| ἀτασθαλίῃσιν ὄλοντο (4.409) | "by … wanton-follies perished" | "perished through … wanton folly" | "recklessness", "blind folly"; follows odyssey-001 (1.7), odyssey-049 |
| ἀρωγή (4.408) | "help" | "help" | "aid", "succour", "assistance"; ἀρωγός "helper" (4.235), ἀρήγω "help" (1.408) |
| τεῖχος ἄρειον (4.407) | "a stronger wall" | "a stronger wall" | "better" (kept for ἀμείνων), "braver" (the table's ἀρείων of men, 2.707), "mightier" and "more warlike" (ἀρήϊος "warlike"); a departure from the table, with the reason: "stronger" is the table's word for φέρτερος, but a wall cannot be "braver", "better" is reserved, and ἄρειον here is the neuter comparative of ἀγαθός in the sense "stronger as a defence", so the one word left is "stronger"; the note names the form |
| ἕδος (Θήβης ἕδος, 4.406) | "the seat of Thebes" | "the seat of Thebes" | "the site of" (the Odyssey's `i` for ἕδος Ἰθάκης, 13.344: a departure, with the reason: "site" reads as bare ground, and what is taken here is the city on it), "the stronghold", "the citadel" (reserved for πτολίεθρον) |
| παυρότερον λαόν (4.407) | "a scantier people" | "fewer troops" | "a smaller army", "a smaller people"; παῦρος keeps "scanty" in `l` and "few" in `i` (2.675), the comparative being "scantier" / "fewer"; λαός "people" / "troops" |

| τὼ μή μοι πατέρας ποθ’ ὁμοίῃ ἔνθεο τιμῇ (4.410) | "Therefore not for me our fathers ever in like honour put." | "So do not ever place our fathers in the same honour as us." | "treat … as equals", "compare"; ἐντίθημι "put in", τιμή "honour" (1.159, kept in the sense "honour"; the sense "price" is only at 3.286) |

The second shared half-line, περὶ δ’ ἄλλων φασὶ γενέσθαι (4.375b = Odyssey 4.201), is NOT carried over: there it is "(Antilochus) was beyond others, they say" with a finite subject, here an infinitive after φασί with Tydeus understood, so `l` "and beyond others, they say, to have been superior." and `i` "and they say that he surpassed the rest." are the Iliad's own; the note names the Odyssey parallel |

| ἐστήριξε (gnomic aorist, 4.443) | "plants" | "plants" | "planted", "set firm"; the gnomic aorist is rendered with the present, as for ἔκλυε "hears" (4.455) |

| χείμαρροι ποταμοί (4.452) | "winter-flowing torrents" | "winter torrents" | "mountain torrents", "winter-swollen rivers", "streams" alone; χεῖμα "winter" + ῥέω "flow", the point being that they run only in the rains |

| κρουνῶν (4.454) | "springs" | "springs" | "fountains", "sources", "wells"; κρουνός a gushing spring |
